label: Nutrition & Dietary Pattern
description: How your overall eating pattern — not any single food — shapes cellular aging, from telomere length to mitochondrial function and gut microbiota balance.

label: Gut Microbiome & Metabolic Byproducts
description: The bacteria in your gut ferment fiber into compounds that influence inflammation, metabolism, and how well your intestinal barrier holds up as you age.

label: Sense of Purpose & Social Connection
description: A strong sense of purpose is one of the most consistently replicated predictors of longer life across large population studies — this is the best-evidenced topic in the library.
sourceLabel: Sense of Purpose & Longevity research ladder

description: Sleep quality and circadian regulation are foundational to recovery — though this topic currently borrows adjacent findings rather than drawing on a dedicated sleep-science source.

label: Physical Activity & Movement
knownLimitation: This topic has no dedicated adult exercise-science source in the static library — it borrows one behavioral finding from the Purpose document and is expected to lean on live web search (restricted to credible domains) for topic-specific depth.
description: Physical activity is one of the best-established levers for healthy aging — this topic focuses on small, sustainable ways to move more, not workout prescriptions.
sourceLabel: Sense of Purpose & Longevity research ladder (movement-adjacent findings only)

label: Metabolic & Cardiovascular Risk
description: Blood pressure, cholesterol, and blood sugar share the same dietary levers — this topic focuses on the DASH-diet mechanisms behind all three.
sourceLabel: DASH Diet research (Nutrition document, DASH section only)

label: Micronutrient & Vitamin Status
description: Vitamin and mineral status — and how genetics can shift individual needs — plays a quiet but measurable role in aging and chronic disease risk.

label: Cognitive Health & Neuroprotection
description: Brain aging is shaped by both psychosocial factors like purpose and specific nutrients like B12, folate, and omega-3 fatty acids.

label: Energy & Mitochondrial Function
description: Mitochondrial health depends on specific dietary compounds — polyphenols, healthy fats, fermentable fiber — that support cellular energy production.
sourceLabel: Mitochondrial-health research (Nutrition document, Mediterranean & Okinawan mechanism sections)

label: Weight Management & Body Composition
description: Weight management here is framed around appetite-hormone signaling from fiber fermentation — not calorie counting.
